pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, Wanderer above the Sea of Fog — one man standing alone on the broken rock at the top of the mountain, seen from behind in a dark green coat with his fair hair blown about and his stick set down against the stone, and the whole country below him drowned in white cloud with the peaks and the crags and the far tower standing up out of it, nobody else anywhere in the picture, blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_wanderer_above_the_sea_of_fog

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Cardsharps — the young gentleman sitting at the gaming table in black velvet and a lace collar with his cards held up close and his eyes down on them, taking in nothing else, the older cheat leaning right over his shoulder out of the dark in a striped sleeve to read the hand and signal it across with his fingers, the dice and the backgammon board lying out on the worn red cloth, and the partner's hand already reaching in at the edge of the table, or set foot on the path of sinners, or sit in the seat of mockers
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_cardsharps

pictures.scene: Eastman Johnson, The Lord Is My Shepherd — a man sitting alone on a low seat in the corner of a bare plank room, in a white shirt with the sleeves rolled back and a dark waistcoat and heavy work boots, the open book held in both hands across his knee and his head bent right down over the page in the one warm bit of light, the rest of the room gone to brown dark around him, but his delight is in the Law of the LORD, and on His law he meditates day and night
pictures.name: pd_johnson_the_lord_is_my_shepherd

pictures.scene: Jacob van Ruisdael, The Marsh — the standing water lying still among the trees with the whole wood doubled in it upside down, great oaks and beeches leaning out over the pool with their roots down in the wet ground, the lily pads and the reeds crowding the near bank and a pair of swans in the shallows, the leaves coming up thick and gold in the light at the top of the picture, he is like a tree planted by streams of water, yielding its fruit in season
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_the_marsh

pictures.scene: John Constable, The Cornfield — the deep green lane running up between the elms in full summer leaf, the flock of sheep coming down it with the dog standing out in front, a boy flat on his front at the edge of the water drinking out of his hands, the donkey and the cattle in the shade, and at the top of the lane the gate opening onto the ripe corn standing gold right across the field with the harvesters already in it and the church tower beyond, whose leaf does not wither, and who prospers in all he does
pictures.name: pd_constable_the_cornfield

pictures.scene: Jean-Francois Millet, The Winnower — the labourer braced on both legs in the half dark of the barn, a red cloth tied round his head, a white shirt, a blue sash at his waist and his legs bound below the knee, swinging the flat wicker basket of grain up in both hands so that the husks fly off it in a cloud through the one shaft of light, not so the wicked, for they are like chaff driven off by the wind
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_winnower

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Christ in Glory — Christ seated inside a deep blue oval ring set with winged heads, in a pale blue robe with a gold halo crossed behind Him, one hand raised and the other open, gold rays going out from Him across the whole ground, an angel standing below with the cross held upright, and the saints and the crowned ranks of heaven gathered close on either side with their hands pressed together, therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_christ_in_glory

pictures.scene: Meindert Hobbema, The Avenue at Middelharnis — the straight cart road running away from us between two files of tall thin trees, the ruts of it holding water, one man in a long coat walking up the middle of it with his dog and a few more figures far off where the road reaches the village, the flat fields and the ditches open on both sides, the red church tower standing at the left and the whole great sky over it, for the LORD guards the path of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish
pictures.name: pd_hobbema_the_avenue_at_middelharnis

lines.text: who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked,
or set foot on the path of sinners,
or sit in the seat of mockers.
But his delight is in the Law of the LORD,
and on His law he meditates day and night.
He is like a tree planted by streams of water,
and who prospers in all he does.
For they are like chaff driven off by the wind.
Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment,
nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous.
For the LORD guards the path of the righteous,
but the way of the wicked will perish.
